prompted_for: Options shown on the equipment they add to (Options with spot icons, later modules on the skid)
composition: full navy blueprint sheet with zone references on the borders
centred uppercase mono headline and subline
six option boxes around a central flow diagram
small skid repeated in several boxes
dashed and solid pipe routes linking boxes
layout_devices: option boxes with code brackets and [+] toggles
dotted leader routes from skid to modules
category eyebrows above boxes (pre-treatment, redundancy, polishing)
zone labels A1/B2 on sheet edges
central flow schematic of tanks and valves
typography: uppercase mono box titles with codes
motion_implied: routes draw from skid to each module
toggling an option adds it to the skid
t2i_keywords: isometric line drawing of process skid
white hairline linework on deep navy
modular option boxes around a central schematic
zone reference letters on sheet border
t2i_prompt: Flat white-line blueprint on deep navy with zone reference letters around a thin border. Centred uppercase monospace headline. At top-centre an isometric hairline drawing of <CONTENT> equipment. Around a central process schematic of tanks, pumps and valves, several square-cornered boxes with uppercase mono titles, bracketed codes and small plus toggles, each holding a simple symbol drawing. Dashed and solid orthogonal pipe routes, some faint steel-blue, link the boxes to the equipment. 1 px strokes, no shading, precise drawing-set look.
signature_idea: Options appear as modules plugged into the actual skid drawing by pipe routes.
strengths: ties each option to real hardware
zone grid and codes feel authentic
weaknesses: too much text and repeated skid images
brand_fit_why: Navy blueprint and square boxes fit, but clutter and all-mono caps work against calm, space-as-material.
